correctness.rationale: With Q the squared physical inner radius and t the weight, the theta quotient continues the series to C×. Its numerator cannot vanish at the simple positive poles Q^k; F′ consequently has exactly double poles there and transforms by the constant −1/(tQ). In a pole- and zero-free pair of boundary circles with ratio Q, the two images have equal winding, giving two zeros counted with multiplicity per fundamental annulus. On (Q,1), every term in F″ is nonnegative and some are positive, while F′ tends to −∞ and +∞ at the two ends by its respective geometric-series tails. Thus there is one simple positive zero; conjugation on the same annulus rules out a nonreal remaining zero, leaving one simple negative orbit. A negative boundary representative genuinely can occur: F_(tQ)(s)=s⁻¹F_t(s) by reindexing. F_1 has a simple kernel zero at −1, so F′_Q(−1)=−F′_1(−1) when the subscript denotes weight at fixed nome, and continuity in weight gives a boundary derivative zero for some t in (Q,1). For the asymptotic, writing ε=√Q gives a locally uniformly convergent derivative expansion holomorphic in ε near zero on small neighborhoods of u=±1/√t: the positive and negative index m contributions have denominators 1+tε^(2m) and t+ε^(2m), respectively, and both have geometric tails. The zero continuation at each simple limiting root has first correction (t−1)ε/t; multiplying by ε gives the stated expansion. The physical range √Q|a|<|s|<|a| lies inside the original scalar annulus for small Q. At equality t|a|²=1 the correction is positive since t>1, selecting just the aligned root, while the strict cases follow from the limiting moduli. The supporting numerical script was inspected, not executed; it is finite corroboration, not the all-parameter certificate.
